title: Proxies and priors: how gatekeeping regimes filter what can be read
description: These claims hold that knowledge evaluation has always run on proxies (journal prestige, citation counts, affiliation) that calcified into gatekeeping, and that copying economies, the Book-of-the-Month Club, modernist legibility demands and peer review installed relevance and legibility regimes long before algorithms. Their present-day versions are classifiers that read literary direct address as prompt injection, a source-relative barrier that keeps an excluded source from correcting the prior that excluded it, and mediation whose losses register as improvement on every metric an institution watches. Forecasts include a market for pre-mediation text, an adversarial arms race against the Mediation Index and rising correction costs against high-prior flattening.
